10.1002_adfm.202516000: Aqueous zinc‐iodine (Zn‐I 2 ) batteries represent attractive candidates for flexible electronics and advanced energy storage due to their environmental benignity, inherent safety, and low cost. However, severe zinc dendrite formation, parasitic side reactions, and rapid polyiodide shuttling coupled with sluggish redox kinetics impede practical deployment. To overcome these limitations, a novel (1,4‐dioxan‐2‐yl)methanol (DXm) is introduced as a multifunctional electrolyte additive. The p ‐band center of ─O─ groups in DXm covalently coordinates with Zn 2 ⁺, enabling uniform zinc deposition and suppressing interfacial side reactions. Meanwhile, DXm introduces p / p ‐π* orbital hybridization with iodine species, accelerating polyiodide redox kinetics. Consequently, DXm‐modified flexible cells exhibit exceptional cyclability and stable performance across a broad temperature range (0–25 °C), even under mechanical deformation. Furthermore, cells employing DXm‐containing seawater electrolyte present 187 mAh g −1 capacity with 1000 cycles at a current density of 25 C. This work provides fundamental insights into p ‐band center modulation for enhanced p / p ‐π* hybridization in electrochemical redox reactions, establishing design principles for sustainable Zn‐I 2 batteries in flexible, wearable, and seawater‐based applications.
10.1002_adfm.76812: A stable zinc (Zn) metal anode (ZMA) is critical for the practical application of aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs), yet challenges such as dendrite formation and side reactions severely hinder long‐term cycling. In this study, we report a well‐ordered organic–inorganic dual‐layer synergistic interface (OIDL) to construct a high‐efficiency ZMA (denoted as OIDL@Zn). OIDL interface is composed of a bottom ZnF 2 ‐rich inorganic layer and a top organic Zn‐ligand complex layer in situ grown on the Zn surface. The organic layer with polar functional groups renders homogeneous and enhanced Zn 2+ flux, compressed electric double layer (EDL) structure, and facilitated Zn 2+ desolvation, thereby enabling uniform Zn deposition and suppressing parasitic reactions. ZnF 2 layer with excellent mechanical stability simultaneously provides efficient Zn 2+ transport pathways and suppresses dendrite growth. Consequently, OIDL@Zn anodes exhibit remarkable cycling stability (over 3000 h at 1 mA cm −2 , over 4500 cycles at 20 mA cm −2 ). A high average Coulombic efficiency (CE) of 99.38% is achieved by OIDL@Zn||Cu cells during 2000 cycles for Zn plating/stripping. Assembled OIDL@Zn||MnO 2 full cells deliver an initial discharge capacity of 231.6 mA h g −1 with a highly improved capacity retention of 86.8% after 2500 cycles at 1 C, and pouch cell tests further validate its stability and practical applicability.
10.1002_aenm.71724: Engineering catalyst‐ionomer interfaces is critical for overcoming the coupled kinetic and transport limitations that impede the commercialization of low‐temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells (LT‐PEMFCs). Herein, a PtCu alloy supported on a zeolitic imidazolate framework‐8‐derived 3D‐hierarchical carbon framework is developed to simultaneously regulate proton transport and interfacial anion adsorption within the catalyst layer. Oxophilic Cu preferentially interacts with Nafion's sulfonate groups, mitigating excessive adsorption on Pt, while the 3D‐hierarchical porous architecture promotes homogeneous ionomer distribution, continuous proton‐conduction pathways, and efficient water transport. Hydrogen underpotential deposition (HUPD) half‐cell analysis across various concentrations of Nafion revealed Temkin‐type adsorption features and demonstrated weakened Nafion adsorption following Cu incorporation, supported by various physical and theoretical analyses. The optimized catalyst exhibits a reduced Tafel slope of 55.8 mV dec − 1 , delivering 0.75 A mg Pt −1 at 0.90 V IR‐free under H 2 ‐O 2 operation, exceeding the U.S. DOE target. Membrane electrode assemblies achieved 1.52 and 1.80 A cm − 2 at 0.70 V under light‐ and heavy‐duty conditions after 30k accelerated stress‐test cycles. Sequential Distribution of Relaxation Time impedance analysis further demonstrates that synergistic regulation of catalyst‐ionomer interactions and proton transport simultaneously mitigates kinetic, ohmic, and mass‐transport losses, providing a general design strategy for high‐performance LT‐PEMFC.
10.1016_j.est.2026.121720: The rapid development of microsupercapacitors (MSCs) has increased demand for high-performance electrode materials that can provide long-lasting energy storage with high power and energy densities. Sputtered iridium oxide film (SIROF) with a platelet morphology is a promising option, due to its superior pseudocapacitive behavior, scalability, and compatibility with microfabrication techniques. In this study, we examine the electrochemical performance of SIROF-based MSCs in a range of electrolytes, including acidic (H2SO4, H3PO4), neutral (Na2SO4, PBS), alkaline (NaOH), gel electrolyte (PVA/H3PO4), and ionic liquid (EMIM TFSI). Comprehensive analyses, including cyclic voltammetry and galvanostatic charge-discharge tests, demonstrate that H3PO4-based electrolytes deliver the highest areal capacitance of 48.6 mF cm-2 with dominant capacitive contributions from both electrical double layer (EDL) capacitance and pseudocapacitance, outperforming neutral and alkaline electrolytes. The PVA/H3PO4 gel demonstrates excellent cycling stability of 99.5% vs 96% (H3PO4) at the end of 10000 cycles. A slower self-discharge of 81.8% is observed for gel compared to liquid electrolyte (80.8%). EMIM TFSI offers a high operating temperature of 60 °C and the highest energy and power densities due to its wider operating voltage. These findings provide valuable insights into the impact of electrode/electrolyte interaction on the overall performance of SIROF. Additionally, the MSCs demonstrated scalable operation and efficient solar charging with commercial photovoltaic cells emphasizing their suitability for integration into self-powered microsystems that holds great potential for advancing next-generation micro-energy storage solutions.
10.1016_j.indic.2026.101170: In rapidly urbanizing African cities, the combination of poor sanitation and growing climate risks remains underexplored. This study examines the combined flood risk and vulnerability of faecal sludge management (FSM) systems in the flood-prone Tandale Ward within the Sinza River catchment, Dar es Salaam. A multi-criteria GIS method integrated five weighted factors: precipitation (0.25), proximity to rivers (0.30), elevation (0.20), slope (0.15), and land use (0.10) to produce flood hazard maps. High and very high-risk zones were identified based on composite index thresholds from the weighted overlay. Validation involved household surveys (n = 308), interviews with pit emptiers, and field observations, which confirmed frequent flooding and sanitation failures in identified hotspots. Results indicate that over 90% of Tandale falls within high to very high flood risk zones, with significant dependence on pit latrines near rivers and low-lying areas. These findings highlight the urgent need for tailored, climate-resilient sanitation strategies in informal settlements.
10.1021_acsami.6c14348: Intrinsic low conductivity and huge volume expansion severely limit the cycling stability of SiOx anodes. Herein, a 3D crosslinked CNT/SiOx-F@C composite is synthesized via bifunctional fluorosilane crosslinkers and conformal pitch carbon coating. Fluorosilane acts as both a silicon source and a crosslinker to build interconnected, conductive CNT frameworks, while the outer pitch carbon optimizes the pore structure and induces flexible, LixPOyF6-rich SEI layers. Kinetic tests reveal dominant capacitive charge storage and a Li+ diffusion coefficient one-order-of-magnitude higher than that of control electrodes. The half-cell delivers a stable reversible capacity of 672.6 mA h g-1 over 200 cycles at 0.2 A g-1 and retains 86.5% capacity after 600 cycles at 1 A g-1. Pre-lithiation elevates the initial Coulombic efficiency from 47.4 to 84.2%, while the electrode achieves an areal capacity approaching 4 mA h cm-2, far exceeding that of commercial graphite. This dual-carbon synergistic strategy provides a facile route to optimizing silicon oxide anodes.
